data.cultural_impact: The name 'Khwazun' has a Persian origin and is renowned for its robust and fearless connotation. In ancient Persian cultures, it was believed that strong and powerful names possessed the ability to bestow those traits upon their bearers. Names like Khwazun were often given to sons in hopes that they would grow up to embody these very qualities.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name Khwazun as the capital of the Banu Ifran, a Berber tribe that lived in the Maghreb region of North Africa between the 13th and 16th centuries. Ibn Khaldun describes Khwazun as a prosperous and powerful city, renowned for its agricultural fertility and strategic location.

Al-Bakri, a 12th-century Arab geographer, mentions Khwazun as a major urban center and the capital of the Banu Ibn Yahya, a Berber dynasty based in the Maghreb region of North Africa. He describes it as a wealthy city with a large population and significant trade connections to the Mediterranean world.
